summary.value: The Kosovo Longcrower is a landrace chicken from the Drenica area of Kosovo, where Albanian speakers call it the Rooster of Drenica. Few people kept it before 2011, but its unusual voice has since made it popular with breeders across the Balkans and in countries such as Austria, Germany, Poland and Sweden. Cocks start crowing at six or seven months, and a typical crow lasts 20 to 40 seconds, with the best birds holding it for a full minute. The birds are black, with a forward-leaning black crest, a V comb and mostly olive-green or gray legs; cocks may show a few red or gold wing feathers. Cocks weigh about 4.5 to 7 pounds and hens about 3.5 to 4.5 pounds. Hens start laying at eight months, produce around 160 white eggs a year and rarely go broody.
